# Module `lune_ui_core::backdrop`

[API reference](../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core`](index.md)

The material seam: the OS backdrop behind a transparent window. Plain data and one capability
trait; the platform implements [`Backdrop`](backdrop.md#trait.Backdrop) for its window type, tests use a null material.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/backdrop.rs:1`

<a id="struct.LuminosityCurve"></a>
### Struct `LuminosityCurve`

```rust
pub struct LuminosityCurve {
    pub mid_point: f64,
    pub white_max_opacity: f64,
    pub mid_point_max_opacity: f64,
    pub black_max_opacity: f64,
}
```

Avalonia's luminosity-to-opacity curve for an acrylic tint (`GetTintOpacityModifier`): a tint
that is nearly white or black is made less opaque, so a light tint does not wash the glass out.
`mid_point` is the brightness (HSV value, 0..=1) at which the tint keeps `mid_point_max_opacity`
of its opacity; towards white the modifier falls to `white_max_opacity`, towards black to
`black_max_opacity`, and a saturated tint is suppressed less.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/backdrop.rs:22`

**Fields**

- <a id="structfield.LuminosityCurve.mid_point"></a>`pub mid_point: f64`

  The brightness at which the modifier is `mid_point_max_opacity`.

- <a id="structfield.LuminosityCurve.white_max_opacity"></a>`pub white_max_opacity: f64`

  The modifier at pure white.

- <a id="structfield.LuminosityCurve.mid_point_max_opacity"></a>`pub mid_point_max_opacity: f64`

  The modifier at `mid_point`.

- <a id="structfield.LuminosityCurve.black_max_opacity"></a>`pub black_max_opacity: f64`

  The modifier at pure black.

```rust
    Blur,

}
```

OS backdrop material requested for the window.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/backdrop.rs:52`

**Variants**

- <a id="variant.BackdropKind.Blur"></a>`Blur`

  Strongest blur the platform offers (macOS vibrancy, Windows acrylic, KDE blur).

- <a id="variant.BackdropKind.Transparent"></a>`Transparent`

  Transparent window without blur (Linux compositors without a blur protocol).

- <a id="variant.BackdropKind.Opaque"></a>`Opaque`

  Opaque fallback (no compositor, or the user turned glass off).

<a id="enum.Material"></a>
### Enum `Material`

```rust
pub enum Material {
    Vibrancy,
    VibrancyFollowsWindow,
    LiquidClear,
    LiquidRegular,
    Custom(OsMaterial),
    Opaque,
}
```

The material requested for the window.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/backdrop.rs:63`

**Variants**

- <a id="variant.Material.Vibrancy"></a>`Vibrancy`

  Light vibrancy (macOS) or acrylic (Windows), kept active when the window is unfocused.

- <a id="variant.Material.VibrancyFollowsWindow"></a>`VibrancyFollowsWindow`

  Like [`Material::Vibrancy`](backdrop.md#variant.Material.Vibrancy), but the material follows the OS: it follows the window's active
  state (macOS; acrylic on Windows). An explicit choice of the app; the toolkit's own
  drawing does not depend on the window's state (R13).

- <a id="variant.Material.LiquidClear"></a>`LiquidClear`

  Clear liquid glass (macOS) or Mica (Windows).

- <a id="variant.Material.LiquidRegular"></a>`LiquidRegular`

  Regular liquid glass (macOS) or tabbed Mica (Windows).

- <a id="variant.Material.Custom"></a>`Custom(OsMaterial)`

  A material described as data, per OS: a new look needs no toolkit change.

- <a id="variant.Material.Opaque"></a>`Opaque`

  No OS material.

**Methods and associated items**

`impl Material`

- <a id="method.Material.is_glass"></a>`pub fn is_glass(self) -> bool`

  True for every material except [`Material::Opaque`](backdrop.md#variant.Material.Opaque).

- <a id="method.Material.os_material"></a>`pub fn os_material(self) -> Option<OsMaterial>`

  The per-OS descriptor this material stands for: `None` for [`Material::Opaque`](backdrop.md#variant.Material.Opaque), the
  carried value for [`Material::Custom`](backdrop.md#variant.Material.Custom), and for the four named forms the descriptor they
  have always meant, so an adapter maps one type only.

## Traits

<a id="trait.Backdrop"></a>
### Trait `Backdrop`

```rust
pub trait Backdrop { .. }
```

Applies an OS backdrop to a native window. One implementation per platform.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/backdrop.rs:256`

**Required items**

- <a id="tymethod.Backdrop.apply"></a>`fn apply(&mut self, material: Material) -> Result<(), String>`

  Applies `material`, first clearing whatever was applied earlier. `Opaque` always succeeds;
  a glass material the platform can't show is an `Err`.

- <a id="tymethod.Backdrop.best_supported"></a>`fn best_supported(&self) -> BackdropKind`

  Best kind this platform/session supports; callers fall back down
  `Blur → Transparent → Opaque` like Avalonia's `TransparencyLevelHint`.
